title: The forgetting reading of the knot test: census, width and the place of parity
claim: Under the forgetting reading of K1-K3, a knot of two loops and a contact is a relation on three variables that is constrained as a whole while every pair is unconstrained. Exactly 34 relations qualify, in five shapes up to renaming and negation, from a single three-literal clause (the atom, 0.19 bits) to parity (1 bit, the most a three-variable pattern can hide). No 2-CNF with witnesses defines a knot; a knot implies no clause narrower than its variables; naming each partial match keeps parity at three literals with 4(n-1)+1 clauses; and every knot of the absence reading is a knot here, while parity is a knot only here.
failure_conditions: The number of two-loop knots under the forgetting reading differs from 34, or their shapes differ.
Some 2-CNF with existentially quantified witnesses defines a knot.
A knot implies a clause narrower than its variables.
The parity chain fails to define parity for some number of variables.
The Lean kernel fails to compile with Lean 4.32.2 or depends on an axiom other than propext and Quot.sound.
A check in check.py accepts its deliberately wrong input.

thesis_alignment.scope: Relational semantics with the forgetting reading of K1-K3 (canonical since 2026-10-19): a knot is a relation over the loops' open distinctions and a contact that is constrained as a whole and unconstrained in every part. 'proved_present' means three-literal relations pass it; 'proved_absent' means no 2-CNF with witnesses does, since 2-CNF relations are determined by their pairs. Which logical structures count as native loops stays interpretive, so the native-formation safe flags stay false.

foundation_claim_scope: Definability and classification of knot relations under the forgetting reading. No native recurrence, composed topology, path, metric, complexity or physical claim.

validation.status: checked: Lean kernel accepted, check.py passed with every control rejecting its wrong input; no human or external review
validation.level: V2 trusted kernel: Lean 4.32.2 checks the two-loop theorems (atom and parity are knots, the hub and the earlier kernel's relation are not, absence knots are knots, no narrow clause, no 2-CNF definition with any witness type) and the parity chain for every length. V1: check.py re-derives the finite claims by its own enumeration, independently of tools/knotlab and of the Lean source.
validation.novelty: known-overlap-found: relations determined by pairs are the majority-closed ones (Schaefer 1978; Baker and Pixley 1975); parity is the binary code of distance two; the chain is the Tseitin encoding (1968). The delta is the forgetting reading as the knot test and the census of its three-variable knots.
validation.independence: Written and checked in one session by Claude at the repository owner's request on 2026-10-19; no human or external review yet.
